utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would like to correct the following: Yesterday, two documents were submitted. The first one which was numbered 111/3 should be renumbered 110/3, and the second one, consecutively, will be numbered 111/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. May we have the appearances, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Niemann, and I appear with my colleagues, Ms. McHenry and Mr. Huber, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: May we have the appearances for the Defence, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I'm Edina Residovic, Defence counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic. Mr. Delalic is also represented by my colleague Mr. Eugene O'Sullivan, professor from Canada. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Howard Morrison. I appear for Mr. Mucic, together with lead counsel Madam Buturovic and Mr. Greaves as consultant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we have the further appearances, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I am Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo, Defence counsel for Mr. Hazim Delic. Mr. Delic is also represented by Mr. Tom Moran, attorney from Houston, Texas.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I am Nancy Boler, and I represent Mr. Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will begin this morning with Mr. Morrison and his witnesses for Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I be permitted to raise just a very short matter about the procedure yesterday afternoon when Mr. Delic spoke to you? It won't take long, but I just wanted to put a proposal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is a matter of concern to us, Your Honours, because I think it could potentially touch upon the broader issue of the trial itself, and that's why I seek to raise it, Your Honours. The difficulty is, of course, that there, of course, can be no protest by any party to an accused person addressing you immediately before you pronounce sentence. The difficulty arises because of the change in the Rules, whereby that can't happen now as a matter of physical practicality. Your Honours, the situation seems to be that if an accused does address you at this stage and does touch upon issues of guilt or innocence, then that immediately becomes an unsworn statement. If it becomes an unsworn statement, then there are certain objections to it, Your Honours. Firstly, the whole basis, as you know, and Your Honour Judge Karibi-Whyte pointed this out yesterday, the whole basis of the unsworn statement was because the accused previously couldn't bear witness in his own case. So the only way he would address the Court would be through that procedure. Because of Rule 85(C), that is not a problem for this jurisdiction. It has never been a problem for this jurisdiction. In jurisdictions where it has been a problem, now it's mostly been abolished, and accused persons can testify in these own cases as witnesses in these own cases. Therefore, it's not permitted when it comes to issues of guilt or innocence. I say it's a matter of general concern, Your Honours, because it can raise issues between the co-accused. It's not just a question for the Prosecution to be concerned about. It does raise questions between co-accused. Co-accused are deprived of the right of cross-examination. Also, it does raise issues which are of concern to the greater public and victims to the proceedings, because things can be put which can't be rebutted or subjected to cross-examination. It seems to me, Your Honours, that a possible solution, which I would commend to you, is that if an accused seeks to address you on questions of mitigation, at this stage in the proceedings, that he be asked to provide a statement. That can then be scrutinised by the parties before he does so. If there are issues touching upon guilt or innocence, they can be addressed prior to him doing so. It's very difficult to ask an accused person, who is not trained in the law, to make a statement and only restrict himself to matters of mitigation. What represents matters of mitigation and matters of guilt or innocence can be a very highly technical and difficult issue and not really something that an accused person can fairly determine. It seems to me, Your Honours, that if there is any further applications in this trial, and I would submit in any cases before the Tribunal, that if a procedure can be adopted whereby a statement is provided so that Your Honours can be addressed and, if necessary, rebuttal evidence could be called. That would be a fairer procedure than to simply allow the accused to speak and to raise issues which can't be contested by cross-examination. That's my submission, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What is your real application, because yesterday you made an objection, and we acknowledged that you could object. I told you the accused is entitled to make such statements if the Trial Chamber allows him to do so. Since it is a statement which is unsworn, it's not a matter which is particularly on the record, as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If it goes to guilt or innocence, Your Honours, this is the concern, because the unsworn previously -- when an accused person couldn't be a witness, that occurred during the course of the trial, and that's because he couldn't be a witness, but that's not a case now. There is a mechanism available to enable it to be dealt with. If he wants to get his side of the story through his own testimony before the Court, he should do so through sworn testimony. The basis of my application is to ask Your Honours to consider inviting the accused in this proceeding, that if any of the others wish to address you, that they do so by way of providing a written statement first. That's what my application is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber takes note of that. Mr. Morrison, you can now carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In fact, the first three Defence witnesses to be called are going to be examined in chief by Madam Buturovic, and then I'm going to deal with the latter three witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. For today, we have called six witnesses in the Defence of Mr. Mucic. I hope that this will not take long. These witnesses will testify exclusively on the character of Mr. Mucic. The first witness that I'm calling is Mr. Velisa Boskovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may take your seat, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: May it please the Court? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Boskovic, can you tell us where you're coming from?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm coming from Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now I live in the former Titograd area, which today is called Podgorica.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Is this in Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you live before?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: For the most part, I used to live in Konjic and I worked in different towns in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: When did you leave Konjic, and since when do you live in Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I left Konjic in 1992 sometime between the 10th and 13th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what is your faith?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm an Orthodox Christian.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: What is your family relation with Mr. Mucic, please?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic and I are brothers-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you are married to his sister?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how long you have known the Mucic family?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have known them for quite awhile, more than 20 years, obviously, not continuously, because I worked in different places, so I didn't spend all my time around them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: How long have you been married to Mr. Mucic's sister?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: About 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in the course of those 20 years of your marriage with Mr. Mucic's sister, in this period, did Mr. Mucic, at any time, as far as you noticed, show any bad attitude towards you, given your confession?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, he did not. It was not in him. I think he liked everyone and respected every person. He was not capable of hating anyone. He was a very sociable person, so he did not distinguish between -- you mentioned different ethnic groups. He did not distinguish between them at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to that. I'm asking you about the period before the war. Was he a sociable person before the war, if you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, very much so, yes. That was his nature, and he was well-liked in any society, in any one.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Could you now tell me, was he inclined to engage in physical altercations?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. He would always take a deep breath, and then he would proceed. In other words, he would always try to calm things down and then try to resolve a situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Boskovic, can you say, was he a reliable person? In other words, when he would promise something to someone, that he would actually follow through with that?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know him, he was always quite reliable, as far as I can tell.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, from your experience, was he always consistent in the sense that he would always react similarly in similar situations? In other words, were his reactions or responses in similar situations be similar?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how to tell you this. It depended on the situation. I said that he was always stable. He was always -- and he reacted in a way that he thought fit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know, was he prone to alcohol?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I believe that he engaged in sports. He lifted weights and things like that. He taught children weightlifting also.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. With respect to your whole family, was Mr. Mucic a person on whom the family could rely?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. You know, he gave advice very freely to everyone. He would recommend what would be a good thing to do or a bad thing to do, what would be a better thing to do and less good thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. My next question is: Was he a person who would lie?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think that he lied, either to himself or to others.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: So he could have been trusted?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: That is true, because he couldn't even lie -- he didn't know how to lie to his own benefit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: With respect to your faith, from that point of view, did he socialise with different confessions? Who were his friends?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as his friends are concerned, he had friends among all groups. You know, in Bosnia, Bosnia is a mix of different people, and he had friends among all different faiths and groups and, in fact, almost to the point that there were more from the other faiths. Specifically, maybe I can give you an example. He was inseparable with Mirko Cerkez and I think that he cried when Mirko Cerkez was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your opinion, was he more inclined to the good or bad, socially speaking?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was always inclined to goodness. He was also very easy to get along with.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Let me move on, Mr. Boskovic. Do you know whether Mr. Mucic was keen on helping people, assisting people, before the war?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: As I stated earlier, he was always helpful. He always would offer advice, and specifically, I can give you an example. I started out in 1988 as a private haulier, and I started in this business without knowing anything about it. He advised me at that time. He would even go with me on this. He was great to work with.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you say whether he was a sociopathic personality? In other words, was he inclined to harm other people?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I think that he would rather protect people. He would protect people more than himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you say whether he was aggressive or was he a normal person or was he a withdrawn person?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: He was a normal person, completely -- a person who had a lot of understanding with broad outlooks. That's how I know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether he was an emotional person?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, 100 per cent. He was emotional, and I'm talking from my personal experience. For me and the children and, of course, his own sister, she was closer to him than the shirt on his back.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, do you know whether he financially supported his family, his immediate family, his brother's family, and his friends?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Whenever there was a need, he did, of course, provided he was in a position to do so. But I think that if anybody would request something of him in that regard, he would always help.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now tell us whether he frequently visited members of his family and his friends?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very frequently, very frequently. He was really dedicated to his family. He worked in Austria and I was surprised at how often he would come back, how often he would endure this. Every Friday, in fact, every Saturday morning, he would show up in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, you mentioned that he engaged in sports. Do you know what other hobbies he had?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Fishing was his big hobby. Swimming.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, did he have any trouble with the law in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that he had some problems with respect to fishing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: I have two additional questions for you. Can you say whether Mr. Mucic, during the war, helped anyone, a person of any faith? Did you hear anything about that since you've lived in Montenegro recently?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have heard -- this is what I'm talking about. I heard that he helped people to get out. He helped them -- he helped them, brought some food. He tried to rescue them. I cannot really speak about it very well because I was not there, but people talked about it. So I heard occasionally, and some of these people I don't even know, but they spoke about him having helped.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: One more question, and it may be a little bit awkward for you. If you don't want to answer, please say so. Were there situations during this period, when you were part of the Mucic family, that Mr. Mucic expected of you to do something and you did not do so, and how did Mr. Mucic react in a situation like this?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic did not bear a grudge. Sometimes there were promises not kept, but he would just get around it. It would be just like jumping over an obstacle, and he would turn it into a joke. This way, he would sort of bring relief to both himself and me. It was his kind of personality.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Boskovic. I have no further questions. Your Honours, this concludes my questioning of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any examinations by anybody?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence of Mr. Delalic has no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: The Defence of Esad Landzo has no questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have the Prosecution any?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: A couple of questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Boskovic, you said that Mr. Mucic couldn't lie and he didn't know how to lie. What do you mean by that, that he didn't have the ability to or what?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: He was that type of personality. He didn't know how to hide his own problems and other people's problems. He never hid anything. This is the type of person that he was. He couldn't hide anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said that he would protect persons more than he would protect himself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We're getting both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I'll try again. It may be fixed now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said in your evidence that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Go and see them and see what the technical people will do. Go and check them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We may test now, I think. Things are back in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. We are working again now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Boskovic, you said in your evidence that Mr. Mucic would protect persons more than protecting himself. When you made this statement, would you say that it applied to Serb people as well as other persons?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: People in general, regardless of -- I mean for everyone, regardless of who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In your estimation, if staying over in a prison camp at night would have protected Serb persons from being beaten, you would say he would do that, notwithstanding the fact that it may expose him to danger?

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I don't know how to respond to that objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I think the objection must be -- I think the objection must be that the question is based upon a hypothesis as far as this witness is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It's not based on a hypothesis, Your Honour. It's based on his record of interview. In his record of interview, he said that he was too frightened to stay over at night --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's not within the experience of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: That's what I mean, it's a hypothesis as far as this witness is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I'll put it another way then, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If I was to put it to you that Mr. Mucic himself said that he was too frightened to stay over in the camp at night, for fear of being beaten by the guards and others in the camp, and thereby not afford protection to the witnesses, would you agree with that statement or disagree with it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Did the question get through to him? I'm not sure he got your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you hear my question?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did understand the question. I don't know how to respond. I did not get the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I'll repeat it again. Do you want me to repeat it for you?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said in your evidence that Mr. Mucic would protect persons, and he would do so, even though that may expose himself to danger. My question is: If I put it to you that he said that he was afraid to stay over in the Celebici camp overnight, thereby possibly affording protection to Serb prisoners, for fear that he might be beaten or otherwise injured or hurt, would you agree with that or would you disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I was not in Konjic. I said that at the very start, so I don't know what went on there. I don't know anything about this, but I talked about him as a person until the war and what he was like as a person. I really wasn't down there, so I really don't know what went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What you're telling us is that you can only speak for him up until the commencement of the war and, thereafter, you can't testify about him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He is speaking about Mucic, what he knows about Mucic. You might know something else quite different, what Mucic told him, but the witness, who is speaking of his own opinion, might not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: He just said, Your Honours, that he's only speaking up until the time of the commencement of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said he worked in Austria. Who did he work for in Austria, do you know?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't. Honestly speaking, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what he did in Austria, what job he had?

utterances.speaker: VELISA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: To be honest, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any other witness? I think -- have you any re-examination of him? If you don't have, he is discharged.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: No additional questions. Thank you very much. I have an additional witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are discharged, Mr. Boskovic. Thank you very much for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: May we have your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask the Court to call the witness Ljilja Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: Would you read out the oath, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please take your seat.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: May it please the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Adilovic, will you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Ljilja Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: What is your maiden name?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: In Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please be more precise as to the neighbourhood of Konjic? Where is your family actually from?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: My family comes from Donje Selo.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, how are you related to Mr. Mucic? I apologise. The maiden name has not been correctly entered into the record. So it should be, perhaps, repeated. What we have here is "Puljenin" with a "P". Your maiden name is Kuljanin with a "K"?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Adilovic, could you tell the Court what you are by religion?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm an Orthodox by religion and I'm of Serb ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How long have you known Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I've known him for about 22 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: How are you related to him?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: My husband and his wife are brother and sister.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Since you've known each other for a very long time, what could you say about Mr. Mucic? What kind of man is he?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: He's a very good person. He's very honest. He's an honest friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how well do you know the character of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I know him quite well, because we lived in the house belonging to the mother of his wife. So we used to see each other very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: How often was it? Could you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: We saw each other every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: These contacts were on a regular, active basis?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. One can say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Did he ever help you in anything? Did he ever assist you in anything? I'm referring to the period prior to the war.

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was always forthcoming. Whenever we needed any kind of help, including financial help, he would always be prepared to help us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: In view of your religion and the fact that Mr. Mucic is of a different religion, did you ever feel uncomfortable in his company? Did you ever feel threatened in any way?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't feel uncomfortable either?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, the contrary. I always felt quite comfortable in his company.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Let us move on. Regarding this period that you spent together, do you think that Mr. Mucic ever had any evil intentions in respect of you?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I never noticed anything of this kind, and I don't think he ever did have any evil intentions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever discuss the issue of ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Before the war, we used to discuss it, but nobody ever insulted anyone. We treated each other as human beings, not as members of a particular religion.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: I believe that you have already answered my following question. However, during these conversations when the issue of nationality or religion was discussed, was Mr. Mucic, did he voice his opinions very loudly? Was he adamant about it?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. This was more like a joke. It was not something that was really important in our environment, in our family.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you say that he had a negative opinion about Serbs?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can claim that he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who was his best friend?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: His best friend was Mirko Cerkez, and he's a cousin of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: How is he related to you?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: My mother and his father are brother and sister.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that Pavo was not prejudiced as regards religion or ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, because he socialised, not only with Serbs, but also with Muslims and others. He had lots of friends.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: You've told us that your cousin was Mr. Mucic's best friend?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of relationship he had with his other fellow citizens? Did he have any other Orthodox friends?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to Mirko, he had lots of friends from Donje Selo, and he had friends from the town of Konjic as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Throughout this period, are you aware of any incident of any people from Konjic who were somehow angry with Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Mucic a revengeful person?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know or did you hear or see Mr. Mucic, during the war, help anyone, anyone from your family or you personally?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: He did help me personally. He helped my parents and he helped my aunt, Koviljka Golubovic who told me about that. She told me that if it had not been for him, because she lived in Donje Selo, and they were rather frightened at the time, that they wouldn't have fared well because he would always protect them, and he even brought them food.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: If the Court will allow me, I would like to ask one more question, and I don't know whether the witness wishes to answer this question. The wife of Mr. Mucic, that is, his ex-wife, does she know that you are here today testifying as a character witness?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. She knows that. She knows that we like him very much, and we told her that we would be going, regardless of what she thinks of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any questions by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you mean when you said the inhabitants of Donje Selo wouldn't have fared well during the war? What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say inhabitants of Donje Selo. I mentioned specifically my aunt. She was afraid of the soldiers belonging to a different ethnic background, different army, and Mr. Mucic helped them by bringing them food, and he was also protecting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, you testified to the fact that Mr. Mucic wouldn't insult anyone because of these nationality, and he wasn't prejudiced to people with different ethnic backgrounds. Have you ever seen him humiliating other people from different ethnic backgrounds, in particular, Serb backgrounds, either during the war or prior to it?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: During the war, I don't know, because I was not there, but I know that he never did before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I take it that you're not aware of any incidents during the war where he humiliated Serb, in particular, one Serb person, because of his ethnic background, in the camp at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: LJILJA ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that, because I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you for your testimony. You are discharged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: I would now kindly ask the Court to call the witness Sejo Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: Will you read out the oath, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please take your seat.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: May it please the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. You may carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you're coming from?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I come from Konjic in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what your family relation is with Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I am the brother of his former wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Are they divorced?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They divorced.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: May I ask you, as a former brother-in-law of Mr. Mucic, do you consider to know him well?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know him quite well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, how long was this period of your acquaintance with him? How long have you known each other?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It has been over 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Did you visit each other?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very frequently. We had a very close relationship.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of such a long relationship and association, can you describe Mr. Mucic as a person?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. He was a person who was very popular. He was considered a person with character and a person who would help others on any occasion. He helped my family quite a lot, and we were always together. That's about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, was he a person of great character, and was he consistent in what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and he also could be trusted on his word.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what your wife is by faith?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: She is Serb. She's Orthodox.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: And you?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I am a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: And your sister married a member of what group?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: She married a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Now, given your situation, that is, that your wife is an Orthodox Christian, could you ever notice that, in the behaviour of Mr. Mucic, that he was showing some kind of animosity towards the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, on the contrary. He even associated with my wife more, and he had a lot of friends among Serbs. Some of my wife's cousins were his best friends. He also had friends among Muslims and Croats. He is a person who never considered religion or an ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, he was almost in better relations with your wife than others?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, both with her and with her cousins too. He had a very close friend who was her cousin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please say what he was like as a person? Was he active and did he look to contribute to the good in society, or was he very passive and a person who was a troublemaker?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: On the contrary. Pavo was always jovial. He was very sociable, and he was making a lot of friends. I'm not aware of any other way of his behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: So this is how you would describe him?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know his characteristics? Was he a man of short temper? Did he do something that he would later feel remorse about?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: If he was short tempered, and if he had any remorse later, that was considering children. There were a lot of children in our families, and if there were some problems among them, this would be the only time that he would maybe become short tempered a little bit, when he tried to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you say regarding Mr. Mucic, whether he had control over himself, that is, over his own behaviour?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had firm control over himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you maybe illustrate it by an example? If not ...

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if I can recall anything now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Given that you have known Mr. Mucic for so long, do you also know his family, his parents and the wider family?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know his family, his whole family.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: In that regard, can you say whether you noticed, in Mr. Mucic's family, on either side, that is, on his maternal or paternal side, whether there were any psychopathic members of the family?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, there were none.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: What could you tell me about them?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: These were people who were similar to Zdravko or Zdravko was like them. They were very popular in the community, and there were no pathological conditions or anything like that in the family that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you now say, if you know, whether you could ever notice that Mr. Mucic, in certain situations, would exceed the accepted norms of behaviour?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, no, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Could you further say whether he was violent, with respect to the persons of the other sex?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, on the contrary. He was very attentive to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: What could you say about him? Was he a polite person or not?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was a very polite person. Everything I have said so far, I think, talks in that respect. He was a wonderful person. I don't know what else to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please say, in your opinion, did Mr. Mucic respect other people? For instance, you, did he respect you and your opinions during your conversations and visits?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: In any kind of debate or discussion, he was keen on hearing out the other side. So he implicitly respected other people and these opinions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, can you now tell me, if you know, what were his positions on mixed societies, given the mixed demographics of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: He was married to -- I think that the fact that he was married to my sister speaks volumes about his position in that regard, because he does not distinguish people by faith or ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: You just stated that you were a mixed family, in other words, you had mixed marriages in your family, that they are different, all three religions represented in your family. How did Mr. Mucic behave in such circles? Was he withdrawn? Did he participate in conversations? Was he a social --

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: On the contrary. He liked to socialise with everyone. He was a person who really liked people. Again, I repeat, the faith and nation meant nothing to him. He was a person who was very popular in any circle of people.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now please say whether you know that he did anything to anyone with any bad intention? I don't know, to you and your wife, even in some gesture?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he did not. I can cite a number of examples when he helped us, but none in the regard that you have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell me whether, on the basis of his behaviour, in as much as you know him, and you said that you know him quite well, could you conclude that he is a pathological person?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Pavo is not a pathological person, nor will he ever be one.

utterances.speaker: MS. BUTUROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Adilovic. Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Defence for Mr. Delalic has no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: The Defence for Mr. Delic has no questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: We have no questions either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, did you live in Konjic during the war in 1992? You have to say "yes" or "no" for the transcript, otherwise it can't be recorded?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you were there, did you hear of the camp that was at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know what it was used for, what its purpose was?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: From that, I take it that you knew that Serb people from the area of the Konjic municipality were being kept there?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Also, I take it, you, at the same time, heard, as did a number of people in the community, that some people were being mistreated there; did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: That they were taken there, yes, but that they were mistreated there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mucic had a position there, didn't he? You knew that?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that he did something there, but I did not know what. But let me tell you, I was a member of the BH army, and I spent very little time in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, would you think that being in charge of a camp which was exclusively used for the purposes of detaining Serb civilians would be consistent with a person who is favourably disposed to all ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I object on this basis to that question. First of all, he's putting an assumption to the witness that Mr. Mucic was in charge of the camp. And, secondly, asking him to comment with the consistency of that assumption. That is simply an improper way to ask a question. It is also an improper question to ask at a time when we are considering matters which go clearly to sentence, because the inevitable inference behind that question is that it tends to support the Prosecution case that, A, he was a commander of the camp and that, B, he did something culpable in that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may address the first question and that is in relation to character evidence. This evidence and all of this evidence so far, has been directed towards establishing that the accused, Mr. Mucic, bore no particular prejudice towards people of other ethnic groups. Indeed, he had a Catholic or universal approach to all ethnic and national groups. In my submission, Your Honours, it is inconsistent for someone to be in charge of a camp which is, specifically, directed towards gathering up civilians and prisoners of war, and ultimately those people being removed from that community, for someone to be in charge of that position, of that camp, and yet to have a universal attitude towards national ethnic groups. It's a different matter if the evidence showed that the person was conscripted or forced into this position. That may present a different light.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't think that is the witness's evidence, that someone is in charge of that position. He never gave such evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, but he's saying, Your Honour, that Mr. Mucic is a man of great altruistic and tolerant views towards people of other ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Towards everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. I'm submitting, Your Honour, that it's an appropriate line of cross-examination to suggest that that's not the case, having regard to the evidence that's before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How are they inconsistent? You may be in charge of a camp of another community, but that doesn't mean that you're not a tolerant person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it's naive for anyone to suggest that in the Konjic area, that this camp at Celebici was there for some sort of altruistic reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Not for an altruistic reason, but for purposes of, maybe, security.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, even if it was for purposes of security, civilians were there, and one could easily decline that position if they had held these views, which was to taken an even-handed approach to people of all ethnic groups and not to want to participate in this. There is no evidence at all, before you, that Mr. Mucic said, look, this is not something that I agree with and I decline to participate in this. I will go on and fight the war but I will not be in charge of this camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It's not going to the matters of the case. You are not really confining yourself to the question of sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: My recollection is that the witness merely said he knew he was in that camp. He did not say in what capacity he was in that camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I'll move along, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Have you ever heard Mr. Mucic use terms such as "Chetnik" or "balija"?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you say that it's in accordance with his character to use such terms or not?

utterances.speaker: SEJO ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, it would not be in his character.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any other examination? If there is none, then I think we can discharge him. Let's have your next witness. You are discharged, Mr. Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Slava Boskovic, please. (The witness entered court).

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: Will you read out the oath, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: With Your Honours' leave. Can you give the Court your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Slava Boskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I think you are the sister of the defendant, Zdravko Mucic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. Yes. I'm the sister of Zdravko Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: This may be a delicate question. Are you an older or younger sister?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm older than him, and he has no other sisters. I'm his only sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: This is even more indelicate. How much older are you than him?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm four years and three months his senior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want you to, please, in due course, explain a little bit about him as a boy, because it's often the boy that becomes the man in terms of character. What sort of a brother was he to you while he was growing up? Once he had got past the age of 6 or 7 and was beginning to develop as a person, what sort of a brother was he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: He was very joyful but still a very quiet child. He was quite obedient.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Obedient to his parents or obedient to you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, both to his parents and to myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: What sort of things did he like to do as a boy? What were his hobbies?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: He always liked sports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember anything specific. Yes, he enjoyed fishing while he was young. He would go jogging. He lifted weights, for example, and he liked to work a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Was he a boy who had a circle of friends?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Were those friends all from the same background as him or did they come from varying backgrounds?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: From varying backgrounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: By which, I mean, do they come from different religious and different ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: They were of different religions. The people my brother socialised with were Muslims, Croats, Orthodox.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: When he was older, when he was a teenager becoming a young man, were you still both living at home?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We spent a long time living together in the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: As brother and sister, how would you describe your relationship? Sometimes it's close. Sometimes brothers and sisters fight like cats and dogs. How was yours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: We had a very good relationship. It was always a very good relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Now, you are married, are you not, to Velisa Boskovic, the first witness who gave evidence today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: He comes from Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Did that present any problems, that you were aware of, between your brother and your husband?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: How did your parents react to your marrying in that way?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: They didn't have any kind of reaction in that regard. They didn't mind my marrying an Orthodox from Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: How old were you when you got married?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: I was 27, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Did you then leave the family home and your brother?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not leave our family house. We stayed. We lived there for awhile, all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: So even after you married, you continued to see your brother and have contact with him?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because we lived in the same house, but we had a separate quarters, separate flats within the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: As he turned into a young man in his early 20s from being a teenager, give us the sort of brief character description of him that you might find on a school report, if you were a head mistress writing to a boy's parents. What would you write?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would write that he's a good person, that he's still very obedient, has no particular problems at school, either with fellow students or anybody else. I think that he was the best in everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Now, in due course, did you have children?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have two sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: How old are they now?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: One is 19 and the other is 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: How did your brother behave towards your sons? What was his relationship with them as they were growing up?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: He always had a very good relationship with them, and my sons like him very much. He means a lot to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Have you, at any stage during your observations of your brother, from the very earliest days until now, ever seen anything in his nature or character that has exhibited violence or anti-social tendencies?

utterances.speaker: SLAVA BOSKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I never observed any such thing, because he was always good natured, all smiles, and I felt very comfortable in his company. I spent a lot of time with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examinations of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We do not have any questions for this Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: We do not have any questions either, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have the Prosecution any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You are discharged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Mirjana Mucic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: Read out the oath, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may take your seat, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: With the Court's leave. Can you give the Court your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: My name is Mirjana Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: What is your relationship to the defendant, Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: You mean how we are related?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: Zdravko Mucic is the brother of my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Where do you live at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: I currently live in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: How long have you lived in Germany?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: For four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Before that, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: In Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: How long in total have you known Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: For more than 15 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Did you know him before you married his brother?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, for about two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: How would you describe the relationship between yourself and Mr. Mucic? Were you simply casual acquaintances or did you get to know him well?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: Throughout these years, we got to know each other very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your family is from Konjic as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Did he get to know your family, as well as you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Give us, please, an indication of the general nature of the relationship between Mr. Mucic and your family, as opposed to you. How did he get on with them?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: He's a very sociable man, and he used to visit my parents very often. He liked to joke with my father, and they always had a very good time together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: We've heard in evidence, and it's not been challenged, that Mr. Mucic had a circle of friends which included friends from other religious and ethnic backgrounds. Did you have direct experience of his friends from such other backgrounds?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes. My brother-in-law, Pavo, has a lot of friends. He has a wide circle of friends, including all nationalities, Serbs, Muslims, Croats. He spent a lot of time socialising with people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Were you part of that social circle yourself?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Did you ever see him, in any way, indicate prejudice towards somebody because of their ethnic or religious background, as opposed to, perhaps, some personal difficulty he might have with them?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: No. He never exhibited any similar type of behaviour, anything that would be expressed in that way towards these people. He liked everyone, regardless of their origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: What would his reaction be if somebody did something that he didn't approve of or didn't like?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: Well, he would try to explain why this was not good, and he tried to say that there were other ways of going about that. He always liked giving advice to people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you the same question that I asked the previous witness, and it was perhaps a question that came as a little surprise to her, and it may to you. I want you to imagine, please, that you are writing a very short reference for Mr. Mucic as, perhaps, a head mistress or an ex-employer, and you wanted to convey to other people, as truthfully as possible, his character. In a few short sentences, what would you say about him?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: That's an interesting question. It's very difficult to put it all in words. However, I can say that he is a wonderful, complete person, and I'm very glad to have a man like him for a brother-in-law, for a friend, a man with whom I've spent a lot of time in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No questions for Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: No questions for Mr. Delic either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have the Prosecution any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mrs. Mucic, did the accused Mr. Mucic ever show you any videos that he had taken in the Konjic area, and, in particular, in Celebici, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Have you ever heard him use terms such as "balija" or "Chetnik"?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA MUCIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: No re-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think the Trial Chamber will now rise and reassemble at noon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We are continuing with Mr. Morrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We are now dealing with the last of the witnesses to give oral evidence on behalf of Mr. Mucic, and the witness Sanda Mucic is being called as I speak.

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: Would you read out this oath, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. You may sit down, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: With Your Honours' leave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can proceed, Mr. Morrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Can you give the Court your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Sanda Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: You are the daughter of Mr. Mucic, the defendant in this case?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Can you tell us how old you are, please?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: I am 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: You now live in Vienna?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: How long have you lived there?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Six years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I want you to go back, please, in your mind to the time when you were a child living with your father and your mother in the Konjic area. How do you remember your childhood? Was it happy, sad, or can you explain it in your own words, please?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: I had a very happy childhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I think you have a brother; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Is he older or younger than you?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: He is two years older.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: As a family group, how would you describe the situation at home? It can be described, I suspect, in many ways, but in your own words, how would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: I was very happy and content living with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: All fathers have to discipline their children from time to time. Describe, please, how your father treated you. First of all, when you were a young child, before you were a teenager, how did he behave towards you?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: He was a very quiet person. He never yelled at me. He always talked to me, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: When you became a teenager, and I think all of us who have teenage children know that sometimes those can be difficult years, but what was his attitude towards you in your early and middle teens?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: He's a very good father, and he's a good companion. I could talk to him about everything. He always provided me with good advice, and I know that he always showed me the right way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: You sound as if you speak of him almost as a friend, as well as a father; is that a fair inference to draw?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Now, your father and your mother are divorced. We've heard that in evidence. When were they divorced?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: They divorced while we were in Konjic the first time, and then for awhile, we lived together in Vienna. I think it was in 1993 or 1994 that they divorced again, kind of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: During the time that you were living together as a family, before whatever difficulties led to the divorce, how did he treat your mother, in your own view, not from what other people have said to you, but from your own observations?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: He was always a very quiet person, and he was always good to my mother. He never spoke bad about her to us, nor did he quarrel with her in front of us. I never heard them quarrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: This may be a difficult question, but can you allocate these feelings to yourself: Who did you feel closer to, your mother or your father?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: I was close to my mother as well, but I think I was closer to my father. I lived with him for the last couple of years, and he gave me all of the advice. He was providing for my education.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: As far as you could observe, as a member of the family, was it the same with your brother? Did he treat your brother in the same sort of way that he treated you?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Was the relationship with your mother more or less difficult in terms of discipline and intervention, that is, more or less difficult than the relationship with your father?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: She was a little bit stricter, but my father never allowed her to really yell at us or to hit us or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Would it be fair to draw the inference from that last answer that he was protective toward you?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Obviously, your father has been in custody for some time now, and you are living in Vienna. What's the nature of your contact with him at the moment?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: We talk quite frequently, and I feel very -- it's very difficult for me to be without him, but we still get along quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Is he still a source of advice and inspiration to you?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes. I still receive advice from him, and I know that he is giving me good advice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Now, we've heard in evidence that your father had business in Austria but regularly came home. I think the evidence was that he came home virtually every weekend. Does that accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I think he was also paying money for your education; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I want you now, please, to speak purely from your own observations. Don't tell the Court anything anyone else may have told you or things you overheard, but just from your own observations. We've heard your father had a group of friends from different cultural and religious backgrounds. Did you, yourself, ever see him exhibit signs of hostility towards anybody on the basis that they were of a different ethnic or religious background to himself?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: I never experienced him say anything like that. He had a very wide circle of friends who very frequently visited us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Has that affected the way that you treat people from different religious or ethnic backgrounds?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: No. It did not influence me. We have very different faiths in our family, and they all get along quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: We've heard about him having a circle of friends from different backgrounds, and I'm not going to repeat that, but can you just think of examples as to how he assisted or helped people who were from a different ethnic or religious background to himself?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: He helped a number of people. I was still very small when we were leaving in Konjic, and he had a lot of friends. It was in different ways. Sometimes it was in money, sometimes it was in goods, whatever people asked of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: After your mother and father had divorced, did they maintain or do they maintain any contact still?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: They had separated, and they would occasionally talk to each other, not too often. They both were working. Regardless of the fact that they had been separated, he still helped her, because in the beginning, she did not work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: After your mother left, after the separation was complete, the second separation, where were you living at that time?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: At that time, I lived with my brother and my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: During the time that you were living together with your brother and your father, but your mother had gone, was there any occasion when he tried to influence you in any way as to how you should view your mother or say anything derogatory or bad about her?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: No. He always said -- he said, "Even though we separated, that doesn't mean that you have to separate from your mother. She's still your mother. You should continue to visit with her." So he never spoke badly about her or tried to influence us in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Again, drawing purely from your own observations and your own experiences, please, have you ever seen or heard your father do anything which was a violent or vengeful occasion when you, perhaps, were surprised or concerned about what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a question which I've asked of other witnesses, and it's going to be difficult for you as a daughter to write it, but do your best. Instead of being his daughter, imagine you are giving your father a reference, that you are his boss at work, and in a few lines you had to describe his character and nature to someone who didn't know him as a person. How would you describe him?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: I would describe him as a very good person, as a reasonable man, as an industrious person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: For instance, if he were applying for a job where you had to be able to trust someone to be honest with money and in his dealings with people, would you feel that you could give him such a reference?

utterances.speaker: SANDA MUCIC
utterances.text: (Nods)

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: You nod. For the record, I would draw the inference and say "yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Defence of Mr. Delalic has no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: The Defence of Mr. Delic has no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: We have no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have the Prosecution any questions for her?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Miss Mucic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are discharged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes the oral evidence that the Defence intend to call on behalf of Mr. Mucic. There are going to be a number of oral submissions. They are based upon the written submissions, but during the course of the hearing since those submissions were written, a number of addenda have emerged, but I'm not going to make those oral submissions now. I will wait for the opportunity for final submissions. They are going to be short and as concise as possible. Whilst I'm on my feet, may I respectfully ask of the Court that Mr. Mucic be excused from his attendance tomorrow? It's for this reason: Obviously, a number of people who he has not seen for a long time have come to this area, and it's going to be his only opportunity to see them as visitors to the prison. He will, of course, still be represented in court. May I ask Your Honours' leave that he not attend court tomorrow so that he can see those people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't know whether that assures that you represent him in his absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. I will certainly be here to represent him in his absence and to look after his interests, as, of course, will Madam Buturovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He can be excused, as long as he is represented. It does not mean he is giving up his right to be present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: It's his decision, of course, at the end of the day, but he is giving up his rights and, as such, he must rely upon his counsel to represent him. He, of course, could have no objection if something happened in his absence, because he has voluntarily waived his rights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He can be excused, Mr. Morrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. As you know, in our written submission, we proposed 11 witnesses to be heard.
